candidates.title: Only child when exalted Saturn rules the Moon sign and receives Jupiter's aspect

source.reference_label: Deva Keralam, Book 1, verse 2062, PDF page 202 (printed page 185)
source.numbering_note: Verse number, printed page, English translation and Sanskrit line were checked on the rendered page image. Guru-nirikshite is retained directionally as Jupiter viewing Saturn.

traditional_results: The text describes the native as the only child, without co-born siblings.
outcome.certainty_note: This is a source match and should be read as a traditional natal indication, not a guaranteed literal outcome.

notes: Immovable Ascendant is encoded explicitly as Taurus, Leo, Scorpio or Aquarius rather than introducing a second modality calculator.
The rule does not inherit the Taurus/Gadaa section heading because the verse itself gives immovable Ascendant as its complete scope.

candidates.title: Secretive sexual conduct when seventh-lord Mars is pressured in the Ascendant

source.reference_label: Deva Keralam, Book 1, verse 2605, PDF page 249 (printed page 232)
source.numbering_note: Verse number, printed page, English translation and Sanskrit line were checked on the rendered page image. The source explicitly allows Saturn's aspect or association.

traditional_results: The text describes a tendency toward secretive or illicit sexual conduct.
outcome.certainty_note: This is a sensitive traditional indication. It must not be presented as proof of conduct or as a factual accusation about a person.

inherited_context.saturn_relation: Saturn aspects Mars or is conjunct Mars

notes: Mars itself does not satisfy the separate 'with a malefic' clause; the additional Ascendant occupant is limited to Sun, Saturn, Rahu or Ketu.
The Sanskrit construction makes the seventh-lord Mars the object: Saturn aspects Mars or is conjunct Mars. Mars merely aspecting Saturn does not satisfy the rule.
